explanations.text:
# COMPILE

user gives an abstraction

ai harness follows [the human skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md): 
  [the run](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:e1:the run)
  registers the project first, and your words reach the tool before any code is written.
  
cli, human init registers the project:
  sweeps the tree through the ignore sieve,
  writes the file list into human/human.json,
  gives the project an id there once, which the training store knows it by,
  copies the reader in, and starts the empty project map.
  
ai harness hands your words to the project map as they are — human map project --verbatim — no spelling fixed, no word trimmed. 
[the verbatim gate](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the guard) refuses a pin in them: 
  the pins come later, when the things they point at exist. 
  the entry is flagged as yours and keeps that first copy as its origin.
ai harness writes the code files, no comments. the gate is static like a compiler's: the file must parse.
ai harness maps the detailed abstraction:
   if for a file — entry 1, a catalog shape, pins into the blocks.
   if a human file, [an abstraction over many files with no code of its own](compiler/cli/human/helpers.py:e1:name_to_map), its pins reach files, blocks, abstractions of a file's map, and abstractions of the project map or of another human file.

[cli refuses a circle over the maps](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:check_cycle) so the pins run one way, down.

ai harness hands your words back with the pins inserted, through a plain retext of that entry:
 [the gate strips the pins out](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the gate on your words) and compares the rest with the words it holds, character for character.
 a changed word is a refusal. 
 pins go in; your words never change on this road.

user rewords them later: 
  human retext project <id> --verbatim takes new words, resets the origin, and marks stale the entries that stood on the old words;
  a sync rewords them only when the code forces it, and says so.

ai harness reports, serves, and arms the watch, so what you write in the reader reaches it — flow 8.

afterwards user can correct with retext, undo, sync — the commands of flow 1.


# READ

user or ai harness runs: human serve, to start the reader from anywhere in the project:

cli climbs to the folder that holds human/human.json and serves it,
           printing the localhost line, the tailnet line, the line that says
           an open training session shows as a layer over the reader, the line that says a new file
           from the reader lands next to the others, and the line
           that says a writing in the reader lands in human/server/ — flow 8.
cli answers human.json with a live file list — a fresh sweep on every ask,
           so a deleted file leaves the tree and a new one appears, no init, no restart.

user opens [the reader](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html): 
  project.json opens first.
  a file shows [every abstraction as one folded header](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:render), the lowest layer first;
  a click on a pin [jumps to its abstraction](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:jump) or it [switches files](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:crossJump) 
  a click on project or human file pin lands on the abstraction and lights the anchor.


# SYNCRONIZATION

user changes the code
user or ai harness run human sync <name>
  
cli runs [a deterministic pass](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:cmd_sync):
  [maps every old line to its new line](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line map),
  [re-resolves every pin and every span](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the re-resolving).
  if only lines moved, return.
cli finds the abstractions the change touches: lines changed, a pin broken, new lines inside the block.
cli writes instruction to ai compiler: 
  the file and its absolute path — read the whole file —, 
  the diff,
  [the project files it imports](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the line about the neighbours),
  the blocks,
  the abstractions to mend,
  the rules:
    keep the untouched lines, 
    keep every anchor, 
    add a sentence for each behaviour the change added.
    an abstraction of your own words goes in [named as yours](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the mark on your words),
    find the smallest edit, in the user's voice.

ai compiler [answers with the mended texts](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:ask_claude), 
runs at the project root,
the instruction given through the pipe and never on the command line, so a long one is not cut short.

cli [gates the answer on a copy](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the rebuild), 
tries up to --tries times. checks if: 
  every block exists,
  every anchor kept, 
  every needed word alive. 
  four failures leave the map untouched.
  
the map gets saved; 
the abstractions that point into a mended one get marked stale:
  in the file's map,
  in every map with no code under it, when one of its abstractions pins the mended one if a word changed, and not if the pins alone moved.
           
shows warning:
  if [new lines landed inside an entry](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the pieces the new lines fall in) and no word changed.
  if [the sync moved words of your own](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the word when your words moved):
the first copy stays in the map, human show marks the entry with [the line that brings them back](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the word about your words).

if user wants to sync the whole project or a human file, [human sync <bare name>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_sync). which uses the old state: git HEAD;

cli asks git for [the files that changed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:changed_files),
re-resolves the file, block, and abstraction pins,
[sends one instruction](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:cmd_sync) for the abstraction that pin a changed file.
           
a project abstraction with the user words goes in named as the users' there too.
the same warning follows when the answer moved them.


# A PARENT ABSTRACTION CHANGED

if abstraction 1 changed by a sync or a retext and a second abstraction points into it:
  abstraction 2 gets [marked as stale](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:mark_children) and a copy of the old text gets added to its json file.
           
the mark is a list. a second changed parent adds [a note of its own](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:add_note),
if parent changes twice before the repair then keeps its first old text. the versions between are the base of nothing. 
if abstraction 2 retexts it still keeps the mark; 
only if repair the mark gets off. which lets the tool know the mending happened and was not guessed.

user asks for the repair: human sync <name> --stale 2

cli writes the second letter: one page for each changed parent.
  its old text, 
  its new text, 
  the diff between the two
  then the dependent's text,
  the rules: mend the words that went wrong, 
  keep every anchor and [every word another entry needs](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:needed_words),
  carry a new fact down at the dependent's own level, pinned at the parent's new anchor.
if the dependent holds the user's words, the letter asks for the smallest edit, in the user's voice.
a parent that is gone stops the run.

ai harness answers with the mended dependent. words only, never code.

cli [gates and saves](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:repair_stale); 
marks the dependents of entry 2 as stale in turn.
a repair that moved words of your own is named on the spot, as a sync's is.
a parent's child can be a parent: the next abstraction layer waits for the users next word, one layer at a time. the layers cross maps too. a human file can be the parent of a human file. the chain never turns back on itself.
a project entry made stale by a file's entry is repaired the same way, each note naming the map and the abstraction it waits on, with the parent read from that map: [human sync project --stale](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:repair_stale).


# TRAIN

user gives this machine its key once: human login <key> — [the sessions live in a store](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the store hand)
           away from your disk, and without the key the training refuses and says to log in.
           A session belongs to you and to one project, named by the id human init wrote into human/human.json;
           a project with no id is refused until human init runs.

user opens a session: human train --open. [Rows without a pick carry over](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:carry).
           A write in the reader that asks claude for a telling — a decompile, a create, an expansion
           with no words — [opens one by itself](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the training of an ask) when none is open.

ai harness, on the next /decompile or sync, or the next such ask of the reader, writes two or three versions per file instead of one:
           best — the catalog shape, with --shape; refinement — for a sync row only, the map's own text,
           filled by the tool, and refused on a new telling, which holds best and free and shows two
           cards in the layer; free — no shape rule. [Each version goes in with its own call](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:cmd_add),
           passes the same pin gates as a map — [the anchors the project map pins into the entry](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:the anchors the project map pins into it)
           among the ones it must keep — and a rewrite keeps its earlier text in the history.
           Each call answers with [the slots filled](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:the slots filled) and,
           on its own line, [the slots still empty](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:the slots still empty), so
           claude writes the missing one before it reports to you.
           An expansion goes in with the entry it hangs from and the highlighted words, one row for each
           such entry, and its versions may not pin into that entry.

cli keeps an open row current when the abstraction it studies is retexted, in a file's map, in the project map, or in a human file by you or by a sync: a row is a photo of its abstraction, and[the row follows](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:refresh_row) with a second photo.
           the copy of the entry's text it keeps becomes the new words, and a middle card that
           still held the old text takes the new one and keeps the old as v1. A middle already
           rewritten stays as it is, and the layer stops calling it current. A store that does not
           answer only warns here: the retext itself stands.

cli serves [the feed](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:loadTrain) as a layer over the reader: an open session covers the page
           on its own, hide puts it away, a line in the bar with the counts brings it back, and so does a new row.
           The session list — from the store, this project's sessions only — and the fresh map come as JSON;
           [a pick lands in the open session](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:pick) over POST, no restart;
           a session of another project is not found.

user swipes and pick — sideways for the versions, up for the next row — and leave a comment if you want.
user closes: human train --close, or the close training button of the layer, which first says what the close will do.
  
cli gives a new telling with no pick [a version of its own](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:takes a version of its own) — best, or free
           when best is missing — and marks the pick as a default, so a write from the reader always lands.
           A sync row with no pick, or a row that misses its versions, is named and carries over.
  
cli [applies each pick](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:apply_row) as a retext of the entry or a new map, then [marks the session finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:cmd_close).
the maps never change before the close.
a pick that rewords an abstraction that a map with no code under it points at leaves a stale note there, one for each changed parent. 
when an expansion lands, [a link event](compiler/cli/human/cmd_train.py:e1:the pin of its target into the new entry) waits for the ai harness, so the highlighted words of the entry it hangs from are pinned down into it.
  
the training store keeps one session record under your name and the project's id, never a file on your disk: 
  the rows, 
  the versions with their shape and history, 
  the pick, 
  the comment, 
  and copy of the code or, for a map with no code under it, [of every file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_project.py:e1:snapshot) under it.


# EDITOR ON READER

user clicks the text of an entry: a box opens in its place, the raw text, pins and all. the same text retext takes — with the caret where you clicked, and it grows as you type.
a file with no map shows one place for its telling and the code of the file under it, and the bar says there is no abstraction yet; 
an empty map with no code under it offers a new abstraction, and once a map holds an entry that place is gone. 
escape, or a click away, closes the box and keeps what you wrote — only the box now open answers a click away;
a click on a pin jumps and opens no box. 
a pin you just typed, one the map does not hold yet, [is read from the target it names](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:guessAnchor).
a pin the page cannot follow shows that target beside the words, and the caret counts past the shown name, so a click after such a pin still lands where you clicked.
typing keeps nothing: Ctrl+S puts the draft in the browser, and the bar says unsaved until you press it.
your words [stay in the place you wrote them](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:keepBox) when the page draws again between one box and the next.
the page keeps its place through all of it: the box opens, grows and closes where you were reading, and an empty place for a telling lights under the pointer, so you see it can be written in.

user makes a file from the page
a right-click on the tree gives the two of them, create file and create human, and the box opens under the row you clicked; the empty space under the rows takes the folder of the last row above it.
if create file:
  a right-click on a folder, or on a file, puts the name you type inside that folder
  the box opens empty and holds the folder of the row out of sight, so you type the name alone and it lands in that folder; 
    a name that starts with / lands at the root
  [the server makes the file empty](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the new file), so it opens on its new abstraction.
  the code comes under your words. 
if create human:
  [the right-click list takes a bare name](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e2:the human file).
  refuse if bare name is already held by another human file or a file at the root
  the folder you right-clicked is kept in the map, so the name stands in the tree under that folder as <name>.human, while its record stays human/human_<name>.json.
  the map opens on its new abstraction with no file under it.
no event is queued.
a path out of the project, into human/, or onto a file already there is refused, with the reason. 
the tree follows the files on disk.
git holds no old copy of a file made here,so its first sync runs against an empty old version.

user asks for an abstraction the user did not write himself, by three roads: on a file with no map the open
           place carries a decompile button — not on an empty file, whose words come first — and one
           click asks claude for the whole-file telling;
           on a mapped entry you highlight words and right-click for expand abstraction, which opens a
           write place on top whose head is the button — your words there, or none at all; a right-click
           on the head of an entry gives create abstraction, a plainer telling over that entry, nothing
           to write. These three send themselves at the click and wait for no compile button, and each
           opens from [the little menu of a right click](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:the menu).
           An expansion is a deeper telling of the words you highlighted: it stands above the entry,
           and the entry pins those words down into it, as a zoom on one block stands above the
           telling of the whole file.
user takes an abstraction away: the same right-click on its head offers delete abstraction, and
           [the head turns into the button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:to take that one away), with a cancel beside it.
           One click takes the entry out at once — this road waits for no compile button and queues
           no event, because nothing is left for claude to do.
  
cli, it runs human undo <name> --entry <id>, and [the gate refuses it](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the gate)
           while another entry, the project map, or an open training row still stands on that entry.
           [The open row comes over the network](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:the training store): a machine with
           no key goes through without that last look, and a store that does not answer, or a project with no id, stops the undo.
  
user presses the compile button, which stands in the bar while a text differs from the map:
           [it sends every place you changed](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:compile), one after the other. The map changes only then.
  
cli takes the writing at the door — [its body read as JSON](compiler/cli/human/__init__.py:e1:the body) —
           and [runs the command you would have typed](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the command run), one per changed text:
           an entry rewritten goes in as human retext <name> <id> --verbatim, a first telling as
           human map <name> --verbatim, and code on a file with no map is written to the file.
           An expansion you wrote words for goes in the same way, as human map <name> --verbatim, so the
           map holds your words before claude works; an expansion with no words, a decompile and a
           create map nothing at the click — the event alone waits. On a machine with a key and a store
           that answers, that event names the open training session, one opened for it when none was — flow 6.
           A file under human/ is refused — the maps take no writing.
           The gates are the ones of flow 1: a refusal comes back to the page in the command's own
           words, named by the place it came from, and nothing is queued.

one event appended to human/server/events.jsonl: the kind, the name, the paths of the map and
           the file, the entry, the old text and the new, and for a code write
           [the pins that reach the file](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:the pins that reach a file).
           An expansion and a create name the entry they stand on, and an expansion carries the
           highlighted words with their pins.

user arms the listening once, from the project root: human watch.

cli [prints every event claude has not finished](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_watch), one JSON line each, then
           follows the queue; --once prints what waits now and returns. An event printed in an earlier
           session comes back marked replay, so claude reads the maps before it syncs anything.

ai harness takes them in order, by [the writing part of the human skill](compiler/cli/human/skills/human/SKILL.md:e1:the writing):
           reads the diff of your words, writes the code they ask for — in a new file when no file of the
           project holds that thing —, syncs every map that stood on
           them, and pins the new sentences back in. A decompile, a create, or an expansion with no
           words has no text of yours to read: claude writes that telling itself and maps it — or, when
           the event names a training session, writes it twice into a row, maps nothing, and the close
           of flow 6 maps your pick. A link event from that close asks only for the last step of an
           expansion: the highlighted words of the entry pinned down into the new one.
           Then [human ack <number>](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:cmd_ack) — the queue
           advances and says how many are left.

user sees the wait in the page: the entry is marked compiling until the ack, because the reader
           [asks every three seconds](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:e1:pollQueue) and the door answers with
           [what still waits](compiler/cli/human/cmd_watch.py:e1:pending). When the wait ends, the page reads
           that map again, so the new words show, and the training looks again for new rows.

cli keeps an open row current when the abstraction it studies is retexted, in a file's map, in the project map, or in a human file by you or by a sync: a row is a photo of its abstraction, andthe row follows with a second photo.
           the copy of the entry's text it keeps becomes the new words, and a middle card that
           still held the old text takes the new one and keeps the old as v1. A middle already
           rewritten stays as it is, and the layer stops calling it current. A store that does not
           answer only warns here: the retext itself stands.

cli serves the feed as a layer over the reader: an open session covers the page
           on its own, hide puts it away, a line in the bar with the counts brings it back, and so does a new row.
           The session list — from the store, this project's sessions only — and the fresh map come as JSON;
           a pick lands in the open session over POST, no restart;
           a session of another project is not found.

user swipes and pick — sideways for the versions, up for the next row — and leave a comment if you want.
user closes: human train --close, or the close training button of the layer, which first says what the close will do.
  
cli gives a new telling with no pick a version of its own — best, or free
           when best is missing — and marks the pick as a default, so a write from the reader always lands.
           A sync row with no pick, or a row that misses its versions, is named and carries over.
  
cli applies each pick as a retext of the entry or a new map, then marks the session finished.
the maps never change before the close.
a pick that rewords an abstraction that a map with no code under it points at leaves a stale note there, one for each changed parent. 
when an expansion lands, a link event waits for the ai harness, so the highlighted words of the entry it hangs from are pinned down into it.
  
the training store keeps one session record under your name and the project's id, never a file on your disk: 
  the rows, 
  the versions with their shape and history, 
  the pick, 
  the comment, 
  and copy of the code or, for a map with no code under it, of every file under it.


# EDITOR ON READER

user clicks the text of an entry: a box opens in its place, the raw text, pins and all. the same text retext takes — with the caret where you clicked, and it grows as you type.
a file with no map shows one place for its telling and the code of the file under it, and the bar says there is no abstraction yet; 
an empty map with no code under it offers a new abstraction, and once a map holds an entry that place is gone. 
escape, or a click away, closes the box and keeps what you wrote — only the box now open answers a click away;
a click on a pin jumps and opens no box. 
a pin you just typed, one the map does not hold yet, is read from the target it names.
a pin the page cannot follow shows that target beside the words, and the caret counts past the shown name, so a click after such a pin still lands where you clicked.
typing keeps nothing: Ctrl+S puts the draft in the browser, and the bar says unsaved until you press it.
your words stay in the place you wrote them when the page draws again between one box and the next.
the page keeps its place through all of it: the box opens, grows and closes where you were reading, and an empty place for a telling lights under the pointer, so you see it can be written in.

user makes a file from the page
a right-click on the tree gives the two of them, create file and create human, and the box opens under the row you clicked; the empty space under the rows takes the folder of the last row above it.
if create file:
  a right-click on a folder, or on a file, puts the name you type inside that folder
  the box opens empty and holds the folder of the row out of sight, so you type the name alone and it lands in that folder; 
    a name that starts with / lands at the root
  the server makes the file empty, so it opens on its new abstraction.
  the code comes under your words. 
if create human:
  the right-click list takes a bare name.
  refuse if bare name is already held by another human file or a file at the root
  the folder you right-clicked is kept in the map, so the name stands in the tree under that folder as <name>.human, while its record stays human/human_<name>.json.
  the map opens on its new abstraction with no file under it.
no event is queued.
a path out of the project, into human/, or onto a file already there is refused, with the reason. 
the tree follows the files on disk.
git holds no old copy of a file made here,so its first sync runs against an empty old version.

user asks for an abstraction the user did not write himself, by three roads: on a file with no map the open
           place carries a decompile button — not on an empty file, whose words come first — and one
           click asks claude for the whole-file telling;
           on a mapped entry you highlight words and right-click for expand abstraction, which opens a
           write place on top whose head is the button — your words there, or none at all; a right-click
           on the head of an entry gives create abstraction, a plainer telling over that entry, nothing
           to write. These three send themselves at the click and wait for no compile button, and each
           opens from the little menu of a right click.
           An expansion is a deeper telling of the words you highlighted: it stands above the entry,
           and the entry pins those words down into it, as a zoom on one block stands above the
           telling of the whole file.
user takes an abstraction away: the same right-click on its head offers delete abstraction, and
           the head turns into the button, with a cancel beside it.
           One click takes the entry out at once — this road waits for no compile button and queues
           no event, because nothing is left for claude to do.
  
cli, it runs human undo <name> --entry <id>, and the gate refuses it
           while another entry, the project map, or an open training row still stands on that entry.
           The open row comes over the network: a machine with
           no key goes through without that last look, and a store that does not answer, or a project with no id, stops the undo.
  
user presses the compile button, which stands in the bar while a text differs from the map:
           it sends every place you changed, one after the other. The map changes only then.
  
cli takes the writing at the door — its body read as JSON —
           and runs the command you would have typed, one per changed text:
           an entry rewritten goes in as human retext <name> <id> --verbatim, a first telling as
           human map <name> --verbatim, and code on a file with no map is written to the file.
           An expansion you wrote words for goes in the same way, as human map <name> --verbatim, so the
           map holds your words before claude works; an expansion with no words, a decompile and a
           create map nothing at the click — the event alone waits. On a machine with a key and a store
           that answers, that event names the open training session, one opened for it when none was — flow 6.
           A file under human/ is refused — the maps take no writing.
           The gates are the ones of flow 1: a refusal comes back to the page in the command's own
           words, named by the place it came from, and nothing is queued.

one event appended to human/server/events.jsonl: the kind, the name, the paths of the map and
           the file, the entry, the old text and the new, and for a code write
           the pins that reach the file.
           An expansion and a create name the entry they stand on, and an expansion carries the
           highlighted words with their pins.

user arms the listening once, from the project root: human watch.

cli prints every event claude has not finished, one JSON line each, then
           follows the queue; --once prints what waits now and returns. An event printed in an earlier
           session comes back marked replay, so claude reads the maps before it syncs anything.

ai harness takes them in order, by the writing part of the human skill:
           reads the diff of your words, writes the code they ask for — in a new file when no file of the
           project holds that thing —, syncs every map that stood on
           them, and pins the new sentences back in. A decompile, a create, or an expansion with no
           words has no text of yours to read: claude writes that telling itself and maps it — or, when
           the event names a training session, writes it twice into a row, maps nothing, and the close
           of flow 6 maps your pick. A link event from that close asks only for the last step of an
           expansion: the highlighted words of the entry pinned down into the new one.
           Then human ack <number> — the queue
           advances and says how many are left.

user sees the wait in the page: the entry is marked compiling until the ack, because the reader
           asks every three seconds and the door answers with
           what still waits. When the wait ends, the page reads
           that map again, so the new words show, and the training looks again for new rows.

explanations.text:
"map it" — what happens between your word and the entry on disk

●  you say the word                                            ([the word](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:cmd_map))
  │     Claude has shown the story and waited. "map it" is the only word that moves it:
  │     the text goes to the tool exactly as shown, through the pipe, with the name of the
  │     file and, for a zoom, the name of the piece it tells. The name can also be a telling
  │     with no code under it — the word project, or the bare name of a human file, which is
  │     made on the first word — and the text goes to that map instead; a name that carries a
  │     path or an ending and is no file of the project stops the run. The pins of such a map
  │     reach wider ([the map with no code under it](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:map_project)):
  │     a file of the project, one piece of a file, or an abstraction of any other map — never
  │     a piece of itself, for it has none.
  │
  ●  the tool reads the file and finds its pieces                ([the pieces of the file](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:block_spans))
  │     It opens the code and notes every named piece with its first and its last line.
  │     It does this for one reason: so a pin on a piece can be given its exact lines.
  │
  ●  the tool reads the pins out of the story                    ([the reading of the pins](compiler/cli/human/decompiler.py:e1:build_anchors))
  │     Every pair of bracketed words with a target after them is one pin. The target must be
  │     a real piece of the file, an anchor of an earlier story, a file of the project, or a
  │     human file by its bare name once that map exists;
  │     a dead name stops the run. Two pins may not share their words, and
  │     no pin may make a circle back to the story it stands in. The circle is looked for
  │     through every map a pin reaches, so a chain that runs out to another map and comes
  │     back is stopped as well.
  │
  ●  the tool guards your own words                              ([the guard on your words](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:verbatim_record))
  │     When the text is yours, given with --verbatim, a pin in it is refused: your words go in
  │     plain, and the pins come later, with retext. A copy stays beside the entry as the origin,
  │     so a later mending can be measured against it.
  │
  ●  the tool writes one entry and never changes another         ([the record](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:the record))
  │     The entry gets the next number, the text, the pins with their exact lines,
  │     and the lines of the piece it tells. It is appended to the map of the file;
  │     the entries before it stay as they were.
  │
  ●  the tool answers you                                        ([the answer](compiler/cli/human/cmd_map.py:e1:counts the lines no abstraction points at yet))
        One line for the entry — its number, its piece, how many pins — and one for the coverage:
        how many lines of code a story now points at. When a check failed, a refusal comes
        instead, in the words of the check, so claude fixes the text and says the word again.
